properties.title: Getting Started with .NET Aspire for Local Development
properties.body:
If you have ever inherited a project, you know how much Aspire decisions shape the daily experience. Small, frequent changes are easier to review, test and roll back. Keep the boundaries explicit so each part can evolve on its own schedule. Measure before and after every change, otherwise you are optimising by intuition.

This article looks at Aspire from a practical angle. A clear contract between systems is worth more than any clever implementation. Make the right thing the easy thing, and most people will do it. Users rarely notice good engineering, but they always notice its absence.

## Common pitfalls

The trick is to start small and let real usage tell you where to invest next. Make the right thing the easy thing, and most people will do it. Most of the complexity comes from edge cases, not from the happy path.

- Add telemetry before you need it
- Automate the checks you would otherwise forget
- Review defaults with the whole team
- Start with the smallest useful version
- Budget time for clean-up after the first release

Observability is not an afterthought; it is how you learn what the system really does. Every abstraction should earn its place by removing more complexity than it adds. Most of the complexity comes from edge cases, not from the happy path.

Treat configuration as part of the product, with the same care as the code. Every abstraction should earn its place by removing more complexity than it adds.

```csharp
builder.AddServiceDefaults();

var app = builder.Build();
app.MapGet("/hello", () => Results.Ok(new { message = "Hello" }));
app.Run();
```
